title: Woodall's Conjecture C(r,s,ch)
statement_text: For every $s, t \in \mathbb{N}$, if $G$ is a graph with $G \not\succeq K_{s,t}$, then $\chi_{\ell}(G) \leq s + t - 1$.
context_text: Woodall stated this conjecture in 2001 in a survey article on list coloring as a list-chromatic strengthening of a weakening of Hadwiger's conjecture. It had been confirmed for $s \leq 2$, for $s=t=3$, and for $s=3, t=4$, but was otherwise open. This conjecture is the central subject of the paper.
paper_contribution: Disproves the conjecture in a strong form: for every $\varepsilon > 0$ and $C \geq 1$ there exists $N = N(\varepsilon, C)$ such that for all integers $s, t$ with $N \leq s \leq t \leq Cs$, there exists a graph without a $K_{s,t}$-minor and list chromatic number greater than $(1-\varepsilon)(2s+t)$, substantially exceeding the conjectured bound of $s+t-1$.

title: Question 1
statement_text: Is every graph without a $K_{4,4}$-minor $7$-choosable? Is every graph without a $K_{3,5}$-minor $7$-choosable?
context_text: Graphs are finite, loopless and without parallel edges; $G\succeq F$ means $G$ contains $F$ as a minor. The list chromatic number $\chi_\ell(G)$ is the least $k$ such that $G$ has a proper coloring from any assignment of lists of size at least $k$ to its vertices ($G$ is then $k$-choosable). Woodall conjectured that for all $s,t\ge1$ every graph with no $K_{s,t}$-minor has $\chi(G)\le s+t-1$ (a weakening of Hadwiger's conjecture, also proposed by Seymour) and even $\chi_\ell(G)\le s+t-1$. The author refutes the list version in a strong form: for all $\varepsilon>0$ and $C\ge1$ there is $N$ such that for all $N\le s\le t\le Cs$ some $K_{s,t}$-minor-free graph has list chromatic number greater than $(1-\varepsilon)(2s+t)$ (so about $3t$ for $s=t$, versus the conjectured $2t-1$); the construction is probabilistic and the resulting values of $s,t$ are astronomically large. Known cases of the list conjecture: it holds for $s\le2$ and for $s=t=3$ (Woodall), and for $s=3,t=4$ since Jørgensen showed $K_{3,4}$-minor-free graphs are 5-degenerate; Kostochka and Prince showed $K_{3,t}$-minor-free graphs are $(t+3)$-choosable for $t\ge6300$, one more than conjectured; Kawarabayashi showed $K_{4,t}$-minor-free graphs are $4t$-choosable, and Jørgensen that $K_{4,4}$-minor-free graphs are 7-degenerate, hence 8-choosable. The author proposes $K_{4,4}$ and $K_{3,5}$ as the smallest open cases of Woodall's list conjecture, which predicts 7-choosability in both cases.

title: Question 2
statement_text: Is it true that for all integers $1 \leq s \leq t$, every graph $G$ with $G \not\succeq K_{s,t}$ satisfies $\chi_{\ell}(G) \leq 2s + t$?
context_text: Graphs are finite, loopless and without parallel edges; $G\succeq F$ means $G$ contains $F$ as a minor. The list chromatic number $\chi_\ell(G)$ is the least $k$ such that $G$ has a proper coloring from any assignment of lists of size at least $k$ to its vertices ($G$ is then $k$-choosable). Woodall conjectured that for all $s,t\ge1$ every graph with no $K_{s,t}$-minor has $\chi(G)\le s+t-1$ (a weakening of Hadwiger's conjecture, also proposed by Seymour) and even $\chi_\ell(G)\le s+t-1$. The author refutes the list version in a strong form: for all $\varepsilon>0$ and $C\ge1$ there is $N$ such that for all $N\le s\le t\le Cs$ some $K_{s,t}$-minor-free graph has list chromatic number greater than $(1-\varepsilon)(2s+t)$ (so about $3t$ for $s=t$, versus the conjectured $2t-1$); the construction is probabilistic and the resulting values of $s,t$ are astronomically large. The question asks whether the lower bound $(1-\varepsilon)(2s+t)$ is essentially tight for all $1\le s\le t$. Known upper bounds: by Delcourt and Postle, $K_t$-minor-free graphs are $O(t(\log\log t)^2)$-choosable, giving $O((s+t)(\log\log(s+t))^2)$ for $K_{s,t}$-minor-free graphs; for $t>(240s\log_2 s)^{8s\log_2 s+1}$ every $K_{s,t}$-minor-free graph is $(3s+t)$-degenerate, hence $(3s+t+1)$-choosable (Kostochka and Prince).

title: Open problem: Woodall's conjecture for fixed s
statement_text: It remains an interesting open problem whether Woodall's conjecture (that every graph without a $K_{s,t}$-minor is $(s+t-1)$-choosable) remains true if $s$ is fixed and $t$ is sufficiently large in terms of $s$.
context_text: Graphs are finite, loopless and without parallel edges; $G\succeq F$ means $G$ contains $F$ as a minor. The list chromatic number $\chi_\ell(G)$ is the least $k$ such that $G$ has a proper coloring from any assignment of lists of size at least $k$ to its vertices ($G$ is then $k$-choosable). Woodall conjectured that for all $s,t\ge1$ every graph with no $K_{s,t}$-minor has $\chi(G)\le s+t-1$ (a weakening of Hadwiger's conjecture, also proposed by Seymour) and even $\chi_\ell(G)\le s+t-1$. The author refutes the list version in a strong form: for all $\varepsilon>0$ and $C\ge1$ there is $N$ such that for all $N\le s\le t\le Cs$ some $K_{s,t}$-minor-free graph has list chromatic number greater than $(1-\varepsilon)(2s+t)$ (so about $3t$ for $s=t$, versus the conjectured $2t-1$); the construction is probabilistic and the resulting values of $s,t$ are astronomically large. The disproof requires $s$ and $t$ of comparable size ($s\le t\le Cs$). For the chromatic number, Kostochka proved that $K_{s,t}$-minor-free graphs are $(s+t-1)$-colorable for every $s$ when $t\ge t_0(s)=O(s^3\log^3 s)$, but no analogous result is known for the list chromatic number; the best is that for $t>(240s\log_2 s)^{8s\log_2 s+1}$ such graphs are $(3s+t)$-degenerate, hence $(3s+t+1)$-choosable. For $s=3$, Kostochka and Prince obtained $(t+3)$-choosability for $t\ge6300$.

title: Open problem: smallest counterexample to Woodall's conjecture
statement_text: It would also be interesting to determine the smallest values of $s$ and $t$ (or of $s + t$) for which Woodall's conjecture (that every graph without a $K_{s,t}$-minor is $(s+t-1)$-choosable) fails.
